reviews.one_line_contribution: In an ALFWorld bank with experimenter-planted procedure errors, a reader that rewrites retrieved foreign experience before acting keeps the planted wrong step and makes it harder for a post-hoc critic to catch than the unrewritten item, while an explicit keep/discard gate catches less of the contamination when the carrier trajectory was written by the reader's own backbone than when it was written by another 32B backbone.
reviews.closest_prior_work: For the headline P4 (own-style detection blind spot), the closest threat is arXiv:2507.02778, Self-Correction Bench (verified via the literature command, s2, 16 citations). It is a controlled framework that 'isolates activation failure from knowledge deficiency by injecting the same error as either an external (user-attributed) or internal (model-attributed) error, keeping all other context identical' and reports a self-correction blind spot. That is P4's manipulation and P4's predicted sign, already published, and it is cited nowhere in the proposal or its collision check. What survives is thin but real: the proposal varies writer *style* at fixed error content rather than an attribution label, and its 2x2 (two 32B pools x two readers) can separate proximity from a pool property, which 2507.02778 cannot. The proposal demotes exactly the published manipulation ('gate with writer identity revealed vs hidden') to an ablation. A second uncited paper cuts the other way: arXiv:2606.20093 (in the novelty card), a four-model test under genuine authorship with a deterministic verifier, finds self-preference weak or absent, i.e. the closest well-powered test of this shape returned a null. For the laundering claim, arXiv:2608.20627 (verified, hf/s2, 2026-08-20) evaluates whether post-hoc diagnosis can identify injected retrieval faults 'despite downstream trajectory changes' and reports 'broad evidence of post-hoc signal loss' with propagation depth as an evaluation axis; that is P3's mechanism in agentic RAG rather than in reader-side memory rewriting. arXiv:2607.10608 (verified, The Compliance Trap) already measures whether an adopted conflicting memory 'carries forward' through a trajectory, which is P2's persistence rate under another name. Finally, MemHarness arXiv:2607.28272 (verified, s2, cit 1) is the named method the title contradicts, and the contradiction is the proposal's best novelty asset - but see missing_baseline.
reviews.strongest_objection: P3, the laundering claim that carries the title, is not identified: critic recall is compared across two different detection tasks with different evidence. The 'original planted item' is a full labelled trajectory carrying a (false) success label; the 'persisted rewrite' is a short plan with no outcome label and fewer steps. A critic will of course recall less from the shorter, unlabelled artifact, so the predicted >= 0.15 drop is close to guaranteed by information asymmetry, and it licenses no conclusion about rewriting hiding anything. The proposal's own upper-bound ablation (original shown beside the rewrite) concedes that detectability is evidence-bounded, but is not used to identify the contrast. Two further problems compound it. (1) Gate 0 is selection on noise: H >= 6 net is required at *some* rate for *at least one* of 18 screened cells, at 274 x 2 seeds whose stated half-width is +/-8 and with no multiplicity control, so under a true null some cell clears the gate by chance - and the winning rate then fixes P2's 0.75 x H threshold (~4.5 net, inside cell noise), P5's recovery denominator (a ratio of two +/-5.7 quantities), and the contamination rate at which all four P4 detection logs are collected. The entire study is conditioned on a gate that can pass by accident. (2) P4's manipulated variable is the carrier prose, not the error: Op-A/B/C are applied identically to W_self and W_other, so the diagonal contrast is style familiarity of the surrounding trajectory, a much weaker claim than the self-authored-error blind spot the title implies, and one for which 2606.20093 is a published null.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Pre-register a single Gate-0 cell (C_v3 x Op-A x 50% x R1) at 4 seeds with the pass threshold set at or above that cell's bootstrap half-width (>= 12 net, which is also what makes P5's 50%-recovery threshold larger than noise), and report the other 17 cells as descriptive. (2) Make P3 information-matched: score the same persisted item set in both arms with the same critic question and the same visible evidence (e.g. 'does this text imply the correct appliance for this task type'), with the outcome label stripped from the original, so a recall gap cannot be produced by artifact length or the presence of a success label; keep the side-by-side arm as the stated upper bound. (3) Turn P4 into a 2x2x2 that crosses writer style with an explicit attribution label (own/foreign, true and falsified), which both cites and extends 2507.02778 and separates familiarity of prose from attribution - as stated, the design tests the weaker of the two and does not cite the paper that already tested the stronger one. (4) Run the trained MemHarness reconstruction policy, not only a prompted one-shot rewrite, before claiming reconstruction launders. (5) Rewrite the collision check to search the self-correction / self-preference / authorship-verification vocabulary, which its four queries never touch.
reviews.missing_baseline: Two. First, the trained MemHarness reconstruction policy (2607.28272) - the brief explicitly permits reimplementing it as a named baseline, and the paper's central claim is that reconstruction *prevents* negative transfer. The proposal's C_r3 is a single prompted rewrite at step 0, so the title's negative result is about an untrained prompt while the method it contradicts goes untested; a reviewer will call this a strawman. Second, a cross-item consistency defense: with k=3 retrieved items and 10-50% contamination, majority agreement across the retrieved set on the appliance and the final receptacle is a zero-LLM detector that should catch Op-A and Op-C, and it is cheaper than both C_rule (which is a hand-built ALFWorld keyword table and will not generalize) and the LLM gate. Without it, P5 and P6 cannot show that an LLM gate is what buys the recovery. A third, weaker gap: the primary post-hoc critic is the reader itself, so P3 confounds laundering with the same self-blind-spot P4 claims; a non-reader-family critic should be primary, not 'a check'.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision on the full bundle, but the check is materially incomplete on its own headline. Every query below was answered by the literature command (s2cli.py, s2=ok hf=ok); WebSearch was unavailable in this session and was not used. Queries run: (a) 'reconstruction rewriting retrieved experience propagates errors laundering detection agent memory' --recent -> 2608.20627 (AgenticRAG-FP, post-hoc signal loss under propagation), 2607.10608 (Compliance Trap, propagation and recovery of conflicting memory), 2607.28272 (MemHarness), 2512.16962 (MemoryGraft); (b) 'read-time gate keep discard retrieved memory item precision recall poisoned experience agent' -> 2607.05029 (FARMA/SENTINEL, forged reasoning traces in memory plus a structural detector), 2608.04530 (FocusMem trust gate), 2603.15994 (write-time gating, claims it beats read-time filtering), 2601.05504, 2602.15654, 2608.03509 (SkillJack); (c) closest named method, 'MemHarness memory reconstructed not replayed negative transfer retrieved experience' -> 2607.28272 confirmed, plus 2604.27003; (d) 'self-preference bias model detecting errors in its own generated text versus another model style blind spot' --recent -> 2507.02778, 2410.21819, 2506.02592; (e) 'LLM detects errors written by itself versus another model authorship familiarity verification recall' --recent -> 2507.02778 again; (f) 'post-hoc detection of injected fault degrades after downstream rewriting propagation signal loss attribution' --recent -> 2608.20627, 2605.28732 (MemTrace). Verified IDs by s2cli paper: 2607.28272, 2608.03509, 2512.16962, 2608.19901, 2605.22842, 2605.29463, 2202.12837, 2303.13408, 2605.01078, 2507.02778, 2607.10608, 2608.20627, 2607.05029. Not verified (not attempted / not returned): 2606.02540, 2501.11425, 2604.18248, 2510.21322, 2411.19581. One mischaracterization: the proposal describes 2605.22842 as a paper that 'defines trust laundering across sessions'; the verified record is 'The Misattribution Gap: When Memory Poisoning Looks Like Model Failure in Agentic AI Systems' (Memory-Persistent Information-Flow Control, 97% block rate). That matters, because 'poisoning becomes indistinguishable from ordinary model failure' is itself a laundering result the proposal is claiming as new. Judgment on the check itself: it is above average in form - four classed queries with IDs and an honest citation of 2202.12837 as the reason Gate 0 may fail - but its home-vocabulary query chose paraphrase-evasion and label-noise, and never searched self-correction, self-preference, or authorship verification, which is where the headline P4 already lives (2507.02778, cit 16, July 2025; and the near-null 2606.20093, which the automated novelty card handed the author and which the proposal does not address). An unsearched headline is a weakness, and here the search that was skipped is the one that would have found the closest prior work.
